_meta.purpose: Cases for byte-exact WYSIWYG whitespace fidelity across the in-app (react-markdown) and email (mistune+nh3) surfaces.
_meta.stage: The contract (this document) is complete (2026-07-01) — the whitespace contract is settled and target_html is filled. Still NOT wired into CI: the assertions become the PR4 parity gate once PR1 (lossless serialization) and PR2/PR3 (in-app + email renderer conformance) land.
_meta.target_html_is_normalized:
target_html is the CANONICAL NORMALIZED, whitespace-tight form both renderers must reduce to for the PR4 parity check — NOT the raw output of either surface. PR4 normalizes each renderer's real HTML (canonical block tags

/semantic, decoded entities, NBSP as U+00A0,
unified, inter-block whitespace dropped) and asserts it equals target_html. Whitespace INSIDE text-bearing blocks is significant and is never normalized away.
_meta.important:
The two surfaces legitimately differ in tags/styling (in-app uses

/

; email uses
+ inline styles for Gmail compat) and in entity handling (client decodes entities; server/nh3 preserve/serialize them). Cross-surface parity is therefore defined on the normalized form above, not raw HTML equality. See README.md and the plan's 'Whitespace contract' section.

status_legend.green: Markdown carries it losslessly through both renderers; remaining work is CSS (white-space: pre-wrap) and/or the cosmetic-\n strip and (for empty blocks) emitting the canonical wrapped form. No serializer/wire change.
status_legend.pr1-gated: Requires a PR1 serializer change (fix a data-loss bug, or emit the settled encoding). `wire` shows the intended post-PR1 form.
status_legend.descoped: Trailing-space fidelity — excluded from the enforced parity contract per decision 3 (the single accepted concession). target_html is null; these cases are not asserted.
status_legend.escalation: Not expressible in Markdown at all (in-cell hard break). Accepted-as-flattened per the contract decision; target_html is the flattened form both surfaces already agree on.
status_legend.rejected: A candidate encoding a contract spike rejected; kept for the record, not a target. target_html is null.
status_legend.control: Must-not-regress (code blocks). Email path currently regresses code blocks (nh3) until the separate <pre>/<code>-aware sanitizer fix lands.
status_legend.legacy:
Pre-migration stored content (old leading spaces, legacy non-self-closing
). Decision 10 — accept, don't backfill: rendered under the new rules and PINNED via in_app_target so future changes can't silently shift how old content displays. Not a cross-surface parity target; target_html is null.

cases.description: 1-3 leading spaces. Canonical encoding is raw NBSP (U+00A0), decided in the contract.
cases.notes: CONTRACT SPIKE RESULT:   does NOT survive identically on the server — nh3 (email) decodes it to a literal space while render_markdown leaves the literal string ' '. Divergent representations => not a safe contract. DECISION: standardize leading spaces on raw NBSP. This REVERSES the plan/audit's 'no client serializer change expected' — PR1 must change the client serializer to emit NBSP instead of  . NBSP survives both renderers + nh3's ^[ \t]+ strip. `wire` shows the intended post-PR1 NBSP form.

cases.name: leading_spaces_nbsp
cases.description: Leading run as raw NBSP — the canonical carrier, confirmed on both surfaces.
cases.notes: The chosen encoding. Raw NBSP survives both parsers and nh3 (the sanitizer's ^[ \t]+ strip does not match NBSP or entities). The  /  ENTITY is not viable on the client (decodes to a plain space) — only the raw NBSP byte survives as NBSP client-side, so PR1 must emit the raw byte. pr1-gated on PR1 emitting NBSP from the serializer.

cases.name: trailing_spaces_paragraph
cases.description: Trailing spaces on a paragraph.
cases.notes: DECISION 3: trailing-space fidelity is the single accepted concession. Trailing spaces are visually invisible and the most expensive case (NBSP-vs-space diverges for search/copy). PR1 does NOT build the NBSP trailing path — paragraphToMarkdown's trim (paragraphFormatting.ts:56) stays; trailing spaces are normalized away as today. Excluded from the parity gate; target_html null.

cases.name: trailing_spaces_heading
cases.description: Trailing spaces inside a heading — incidentally preserved today.
cases.notes: Headings incidentally keep trailing whitespace because paragraphToMarkdown's trim only touches paragraphs. Under decision 3 trailing fidelity is not guaranteed anywhere, so this is excluded from the parity gate (target_html null) even though the surfaces happen to agree today. Proves the model CAN carry trailing whitespace if the concession is ever revisited.

cases.description: Shift+Enter serialized as the Markdown hard-break token — the CHOSEN single-break encoding.
cases.notes:
CONTRACT DECISION: keep the hard-break token. It round-trips losslessly through the editor (parse -> paragraph[text, hard_break, text]; verified by the contract client spike). It renders
PLUS a cosmetic (the PR-8561 mechanism) which DOUBLES the break under pre-wrap — so PR2 (rehype) and PR3 (post-render) must strip the adjacent to

cases.description:
REJECTED candidate: serialize Shift+Enter as inline
instead of the token.

observed.in_app_html: PARSED TO A SINGLE EMPTY PARAGRAPH, 'a' and 'b' DROPPED — silent data loss.

cases.notes:
CONTRACT SPIKE RESULT (rejected): inline
renders clean on the SERVER (no cosmetic \n), but on the CLIENT it causes silent DATA LOSS. breaksToEmptyParagraphs (paragraphFormatting.ts:9) matches any
html node regardless of block/inline position and splices an illegal block inside the paragraph; prosemirror-remark then degrades the whole paragraph to one empty paragraph, dropping the surrounding text. Usable only if PR1 first fixes breaksToEmptyParagraphs to be block-level-only, then re-verifies — higher risk than the token. Rejected in favor of single_hard_break_token.

cases.name: hard_break_heading
cases.description: Hard break inside a heading — structural + latent round-trip bug.
cases.notes:
BUG (fixed in PR1): serialize() previously emitted a setext '=' underline ("H\\\nx\n=\n") that re-parsed to an EMPTY doc — heading + Shift+Enter lost everything on reload. Mechanism (verified 2026-07-01): mdast-util-to-markdown's formatHeadingAsSetext FORCE-selects setext when an h1/h2 contains a break node (literalWithBreak), regardless of the setext:false config. PR1 RESOLUTION (decision, Nick 2026-07-01): the plan's 'ATX + inline break' is empirically unachievable — an inline
in a heading triggers breaksToEmptyParagraphs data loss on parse, and an ATX heading cannot hold a real newline. So flattenHeadingBreaks (markNormalization.ts) replaces an in-heading break with a SPACE, forcing ATX ('# H x') which round-trips losslessly with NO data loss. The visible
is an accepted fidelity loss (in-heading breaks are rare), mirroring hard_break_table_cell. `wire` and target_html are the flattened ATX form.

cases.name: code_block_all_whitespace
cases.description: Fenced code block whose body is ONLY whitespace (spaces + a blank line).
cases.notes: REGRESSION GUARD for the cosmetic-\n strip's <pre>/<code> exemption. Code content is verbatim and exempt from ALL whitespace handling (contract; normalization rule 5). rehypeStripBreakNewlines must NOT descend into <pre>/<code> — an all-whitespace code block is a single whitespace-only text node that would otherwise match the strip's cosmetic-newline regex and be deleted (silent data loss inside code). in_app_target pins the verbatim body. Cross-surface code parity is covered by code_block_fenced; target_html null here (this guards the in-app strip, and the email path's all-whitespace behavior awaits the separate nh3 <pre>/<code> fix).

cases.name: soft_break_paragraph
cases.description: A markdown soft line break (bare newline inside a paragraph), not the hard-break token.

observed.in_app_html:
a b

(soft break kept as an embedded newline)

cases.notes: PINS THE SOFT-BREAK DECISION (kept, not stripped). A soft break renders as a newline EMBEDDED in a mixed text node ('a\nb'), never as the standalone whitespace-only node rehypeStripBreakNewlines targets — so the strip leaves it verbatim and pre-wrap shows it as a single line break. This is intentional fidelity (the author's newline), distinct from the cosmetic \n a hard break emits. Not editor output (the editor serializes single breaks as the hard-break token); target_html null.

cases.name: em_soft_em
cases.description: A soft line break BETWEEN two adjacent inline elements (*foo*\n*bar*), not the hard-break token.

observed.in_app_html:
foo bar

(soft break kept as a standalone newline node between the two siblings)

cases.notes: REGRESSION GUARD for the position-aware cosmetic-\n strip. A soft break between two inline elements is a STANDALONE whitespace-only newline node (p[em, "\n", em]) - the same shape as the cosmetic hard-break/inter-block newline the strip removes. rehypeStripBreakNewlines must NOT strip it: it is authored content and pre-wrap renders it as the intended line break. Stripping it welds the spans into foobar (renders "foobar") - the bug bencrouse flagged on PR #8732. Distinct from soft_break_paragraph, where the newline stays embedded in a mixed text node. Not editor output (single breaks serialize as the hard-break token); target_html null.
